title: Affine spin-pencil factorization of generalized driven anisotropic Rabi--Stark Hamiltonians in an inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra
authors: B. M. Rodriguez-Lara, F. H. Maldonado-Villamizar, A. Kafuri, A. Moroz
abstract: We construct a supersymmetric factorization for generalized driven anisotropic Rabi--Stark Hamiltonians using an affine factor $\hat{A}=\hat{C}+\hat{a}\hat{D}$ in an inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra, with two real invertible spin matrices $\hat{C}$ and $\hat{D}$. The six real pencil parameters constrain nine Hamiltonian frequencies and one energy offset up to an overall frequency scale. The normal product $\hat{A}^{\dagger}\hat{A}$ has an exact zero-energy ground doublet and, with its antinormal partner $\hat{A}\hat{A}^{\dagger}$, gives a Witten index of two. For distinct pencil roots with finite baseline slopes, coherent gauges define a Bargmann hierarchy and endpoint conditions for exceptional finite-polynomial states. The spin grading organizes four limiting cases, comprising two driven-oscillator families with every baseline exact and the constrained anisotropic-Rabi and Rabi--Stark sheets, which meet at the degenerate-qubit isotropic Rabi model. An aligned interior example adds direct and longitudinal drives, Stark deformation, and intensity-dependent coupling while retaining the factorization.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a supersymmetric factorization method for complex Rabi-Stark Hamiltonians using the inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra. By analyzing the structure via an affine factor, the authors characterize the system's spectral properties across multiple physical limits. This provides a powerful algebraic tool for understanding driven quantum optical systems.
main_problem: The paper constructs a supersymmetric factorization for generalized driven anisotropic Rabi--Stark Hamiltonians.
main_result: The factorization successfully characterizes the spectral structure across various parameter regimes, yielding a factor index of two and defining coherent-gauge baselines for the energy spectrum.
method: The analysis employs an affine factor $\hat{A} = \hat{C} + \hat{a} \hat{D}$ within the inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra $\mathfrak{hosp}(2|2)$ to derive factorized Hamiltonians $\hat{H}_{\pm} = \hat{A}^{\dagger}\hat{A}$ and $\hat{A}\hat{A}^{\dagger}$.
model_or_system: The model concerns generalized driven anisotropic Rabi--Stark Hamiltonians, which are analyzed using the algebraic framework of $\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)$ embedded in $\mathfrak{hosp}(2|2)$. The system relates to quantum Rabi models relevant in platforms like trapped-ion simulations.
key_observables: Zero-energy ground doublet, Witten index of two, coherent-gauge baselines, and the finite-Fock spectrum.
important_parameters: Six real pencil parameters constrain the system, defining various limiting cases including the isotropic Rabi model and driven-oscillator families.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the invertibility of the spin matrices $\hat{C}$ and $\hat{D}$ and relies on matching coefficients in the Bargmann differential equation hierarchy to determine baselines.
figures_summary: Figures compare the finite-Fock spectrum on different factorization sheets (Identity–exchange, Exchange–exchange, Interior) against the derived coherent-gauge baselines.
paper_structure: The paper develops from standard Rabi models to the full quantum Rabi model, embedding the structure into $\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)$, and finally extending the analysis to the inhomogeneous algebra $\mathfrak{hosp}(2|2)$ using the spin-pencil factorization.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep algebraic and structural understanding of complex quantum coupling models (Rabi-Stark), which are central to controlling quantum interactions in modern AMO platforms like trapped ions and superconducting circuits.
